arrive.text: A runaway trolley again. This time, you're on a bridge above the line.

five.text: Five people, working on the track ahead. They can't hear it coming.

big.text: Beside you, a very large man, leaning on the railing.

ask.text: If he fell in front of the trolley, it would stop. Would you push him?

too_light.text: You look over the edge. You're too light to stop it. Only he is heavy enough.

pushed_1.text: He stopped the trolley. The five are safe.

pushed_2.text: One life for five, the same trade as the lever. But this time you had to put your hands on him.

stayed_1.text: You didn't push. The trolley went under the bridge, and on to the five.

stayed_2.text: Most people would pull the lever, but won't push. The numbers didn't change. So what did?

again_diff.text: This time, you chose the other way.

end.text: Steering the trolley past someone feels different from using them to stop it. Even when the numbers are the same.
